The annual securities report states that, even though sales volume fell, cost control through production management matched to demand, productivity improvements and yield improvement kept the gross profit margin at 18.7%, the same as the previous year. The Company is in charge of it. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥3,808 million (down 4.0% from the same period of the previous year), and segment operating profit was ¥320 million (down 0.2%). The securities report states that demand for nails fell because of the decrease in new housing starts and the Company's sales volume also fell from the previous fiscal year, while wooden buildings in the non-residential field tend to increase under the policy of using domestic timber. Profit stayed almost level with the previous fiscal year through optimization of the product mix between overseas OEM products and domestically produced products and through fixed cost reductions.

entries.ff6a7cf205fa57ac: In December 1949, when Daiken Sangyo Co., Ltd. was split into 4 companies under a reconstruction and reorganization plan, it started as Amagasaki Seitetsusho Co., Ltd., at the same time as the current Marubeni Corporation, Itochu Corporation and others. The annual securities report describes the circumstances of its founding as follows: Kishimoto Iron Works, established in Amagasaki in 1901, was the company's earliest predecessor; in May 1911 it separated and became independent as Kishimoto Seitetsusho Partnership Company; in May 1937 it was reorganized into Amagasaki Seitetsusho Co., Ltd.; in September 1941 it merged with Marubeni Shoten Co., Ltd. and others to become Sanko Co., Ltd.; and in September 1944 Daiken Sangyo Co., Ltd. was established.
